newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kuchma reshuffles Ukraine cabinet to speed reforms.
newsitem.headline: Kuchma reshuffles Ukraine cabinet to speed reforms.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma, trying to speed up Ukraine's sluggish economic reforms, on Friday radically reshuffled his government following the appointment of a new pragmatic prime minister earlier this month.
Kuchma issued decrees replacing the ministers overseeing key areas of reform including the economy, industry and energy portfolios.

"The government reshuffle, together with the appointment of a new prime minister (earlier this month) were the result of the president's desire to accelerate economic reforms," Kuchma's spokesman Petro Ostapenko told Reuters by telephone.
He said Viktor Suslov, who heads the parliamentary banking and finance committee, had been appointed as new economy minister, replacing Yuri Yekhanurov.
Kuchma also appointed Yuri Karasyk to head the agriculture ministry, a post he has held before, replacing Mykhailo Zubets.
The other sacked ministers were energy minister Yuri Bochkaryov, coal mining minister Yuri Rusantsov and industry minister Valery Mazur.
More new appointments, along with decrees on the structure of the government, were due to be announced later on Friday, Ostapenko said.

He added that Defence Minister Olexander Kuzmuk, Interior Minister Yuri Kravchenko, Finance Minister Ihor Mityukov and Deputy Prime Minister in charge of reforms Serhiy Tyhypko had retained their posts in the reshuffle.
New Prime Minister Valery Pustovoitenko was appointed on July 16 following the resignation of the former head of the government, Pavlo Lazarenko.
Under Ukraine's constitution, Kuchma is obliged to form a new cabinet following the appointment of a new head of government.
